gates._ceiling_raise_130: analytics_consent_check.mjs — 2026-09-03. His two rulings the same evening: analytics on the game, About and Rules only, and cookieless with no banner. The property is an ORDER, not a presence: every wrong version of this looks correct, because the tag is there and the denial is there and the denial arrives after the tag has already decided it may store. So the gate RUNS the installer against a fake window and watches the sequence, rather than grepping for a snippet. THE ERROR THAT NOTE MADE IS THE ONE THIS GATE EXISTS TO PREVENT ANYONE MAKING AGAIN: a sitemap is an invitation, not a fence, so leaving a page out of it changes nothing about whether a crawler may read and index it. THE SET IT GUARDS ALREADY GREW WHILE THE RULING SAT UNACTIONED -- scratchpad/ did not exist when he ruled and carries two more pages today -- which is exactly why the gate DERIVES both sets rather than holding a list: the served set comes from git ls-files minus the path segments Jekyll drops (this repo has no .nojekyll and no _config.yml, verified), and the public set is parsed out of sitemap.xml's own <loc> elements, so a page committed tomorrow is covered the day it lands. MEASURED AGAINST THE LIVE DOMAIN, NOT THE REPO FILE: /art-review/gallery.html answers 200 and /.planning/playtest-checklist.html answers 404, which is what proved the ruling's parenthetical claim about nineteen .planning files FALSE and its headline count of thirteen exactly RIGHT. RED-PROOFED FIVE WAYS, BUILT IN AS --red= MODES so anyone can re-run them without write access (CEO 183 could not audit the first version because breaking it required editing a page): nometa, bodymeta, publicnoindex, unfenced, newfolder. Every one trips, and a mode that changes nothing exits 2 rather than passing. TWO REAL DEFECTS CAME OUT OF RED-PROOFING RATHER THAN OUT OF REVIEW. (1) The failure advice told the reader to ADD noindex when the fault was a PUBLIC page wrongly marked noindex -- the exact opposite of the fix -- so the hint is now chosen by which clause failed. (2) FAR WORSE: once robots.txt fenced /art-review/ with per-page Allow overrides, a naive Disallow-only reader treated all thirteen already-live pages as fenced and STOPPED REQUIRING THE NOINDEX THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF THEM -- the gate had quietly disarmed itself, and --red=nometa reporting 'changed nothing' is the only reason anyone noticed. It now implements longest-match-wins (RFC 9309). CLAUSE 2 EXISTS BECAUSE THE FIRST VERSION GLOBBED *.html AND COULD THEREFORE NEVER SEE 376 SERVED FILES UNDER scripts/ -- a folder Wyatt named BY NAME (CEO 183, finding 1). A .js, .png or .md has no head to carry a meta and Pages cannot send an X-Robots-Tag, so robots.txt is the only tool for them; clause 2 classifies every top-level folder SHIPPED (assets, src, sfx, classic -- the game, which a crawler must be able to render) or WORKING (fenced), and is STRICT BY DEFAULT, so a folder nobody has classified FAILS. The fix splits by tool for a measured reason: noindex in the page for anything ALREADY LIVE (a Disallow stops the crawler fetching, so it can never read a noindex and never drops a URL it already holds), Disallow for whole working folders, and Allow overrides so the thirteen stay fetchable long enough to be told to leave.

_ceiling_raise_2026_09_02d: 105 -> 106, deliberately, for detached_trial_windowless_check.mjs. quiet_gate_report.mjs offers ZERO retirement candidates for the third raise running (0 of 18, every one touched inside five days), so the ceiling was raised rather than a live per-bug gate traded away. What it buys: Wyatt saw a black node.exe console appear on the Blade and asked what it was -- it is a sea trial, and its X kills an 85-minute run silently. Measured cause (INBOX-20260901T1440Z, and NOT the one that entry guessed): a detached process has no console at all, so on Windows every console child it spawns is given a BRAND-NEW console, which is a visible window. The gate proves the fix BOTH ways on Windows -- a child spawned without windowsHide must show a visible window, or the check declares itself blind rather than passing -- and derives its coverage half by scanning sea_trial.mjs, so a spawn site added next month fails the build instead of opening a window next release.
